title: Monte Carlo Probability Workbench
summary: Model a practical problem, check its assumptions and compare decisions with Monte Carlo simulation. Groups 1 to 3 of 10: the 10 discrete, 13 continuous and 16 positive, heavy-tailed and extreme-value laws (lognormal to stable, GEV, GPD, Gumbel and reverse Weibull), each with a behaviour experiment and three workflows of its own; censored observations; tail plots and the exact laws of maxima and sums; independent sampling, the inverse transform and rejection sampling; stratification, antithetic variables, control variates and common random numbers; a Philox4x32-10 generator with named streams and workers, exact or numerical reference values, claim tags for every result, and versioned model and run records. Four public-domain datasets: Bortkiewicz's horse kicks, Rutherford and Geiger's alpha particles, Weldon's dice and the annual rainfall maxima of Fort Collins. Works offline: MathJax 4.1.3 and Fira Math are embedded.
